messages.subject: SIZE OF THE SEGMENTS
parts:
Dear all,

 

We are building a Density Surface Model with line transects. We have 8000km of transects in a large area and our truncation distance was 500m. If we follow the recommendations of the segment size, we will have a very large number of segments (8000 Segments). Thus, we were wondering if there are possible future complications in the analysis if we consider segments of 5km. The area is fairly homogeneous, so the segment would not varied too much with each other and the study specie have huge home range.

 

Thanks a lot for your help and time


Julieta

Julieta

It seems you have given thought to the issue of homogeneity within segments and animal characteristics.   The other issue that is of relevance is the spatial measurement resolution of the covariates you intend to include.  Others may have additional thoughts for you.

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] SIZE OF THE SEGMENTS
parts:
Hi Julieta, listfolk,

Just to echo Mikhail's point here, there are folks I speak to routinely
running analyses in the order of hundreds of thousands of segments. If
you have sufficient computing power and begin with a relatively simple
model, this should work. It's worth starting out very simple (just a
smooth of 1 or 2 covariates) and time your model to see what kind of
time scale you'll need to work on. Code like

> a<-Sys.time()

# run your model

> b<-Sys.time()
> b-a # obtain difference

can get you that number.

Hope that helps.


cheers,
--dave
